title: BoundedCompositeSaddle.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Both g on X and h on Y are convex; the objective is convex in x and concave in y. Strong convexity is not assumed.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Find an approximate saddle point of Φ(x,y)=g(x)+⟨y,Kx⟩−h(y) over X×Y.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: A bounded bilinear coupling is combined with possibly nonsmooth convex terms accessed through separate constrained proximal maps.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact minimizers of ηg(x)+‖x−a‖²/2 over X and ηh(y)+‖y−b‖²/2 over Y are available for every center and every η>0. Each query counts as one oracle call.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact applications of K and its adjoint are separate oracle queries. All four reply types are independent of the call index and oracle seed; no function-value or subgradient oracle is supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are real inner-product spaces, without completeness or finite-dimensionality assumptions. X and Y are convex, nonempty, and contained in radius-R balls; closedness is not explicitly assumed. Exact proximal minimizers and an everywhere-defined adjoint are explicitly required. Public information includes X,Y,x0,y0,R,L,M,ε, with R,L,ε>0 and M≥0. The hidden instance satisfies ‖K‖≤L and g,h are M-Lipschitz on their respective feasible sets. The permitted algorithm family is specified by spec.allowedAlgorithm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BoundedCompositeSaddle.lean: Public, Problem, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible, spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: saddle_point_gap
accuracy.details: The output (x̄,ȳ) must satisfy Φ(x̄,y)−Φ(x,ȳ)≤ε simultaneously for every x∈X and y∈Y.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned pair must belong to X×Y.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the uniform ε saddle-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law. The oracle-call budget is a fixed bound holding for every seed.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard bounded convex-concave bilinear composite saddle problem with exact proximal and linear-operator access and a uniform saddle-gap criterion. Its formulation allows general inner-product spaces and explicitly assumes proximal solvability.

descriptionHtml:
Arrow–Hurwicz for Bounded Composite Saddles

We consider the saddle objective Φ(x,y)=g(x)+⟨y,Kx⟩−h(y) on convex sets X⊂E and Y⊂F, where E,F are real inner product spaces. Both sets lie in balls of radius R>0 about zero; g:E→R and h:F→R are convex and M-Lipschitz on their respective sets, with M≥0, and K:E→F is bounded linear with operator norm at most L>0. The oracle returns exact linear-map, adjoint, and constrained proximal evaluations. From given feasible points, Arrow–Hurwicz must return a feasible pair (x¯,y¯) satisfying Φ(x¯,y)−Φ(x,y¯)≤ε for every (x,y)∈X×Y, almost surely, where ε>0 is the tolerance.

The optimization problem is infx∈Xsupy∈YΦ(x,y). The norms on E and F are induced by their inner products, and we use the product norm ∥(x,y)∥=max{∥x∥,∥y∥}. Operator norms are the induced operator norms. The algorithm receives E,F,X,Y,R,L,M,ε and the starting points x0,y0; access to K,g,h is through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Bounded feasible sets). The sets X and Y are convex, x0∈X, y0∈Y, and ∥x∥≤Rfor every x∈X,∥y∥≤Rfor every y∈Y.

Assumption 2 (Convex composite objective). The functions g and h are convex on X and Y, respectively, and satisfy |g(a)−g(b)|≤M∥a−b∥(a,b∈X),|h(a)−h(b)|≤M∥a−b∥(a,b∈Y). The map K:E→F is bounded linear with ∥K∥op≤L. There exists a map K∗:F→E satisfying ⟨K∗y,z⟩=⟨y,Kz⟩,y∈F, z∈E.

Assumption 3 (Exact proximal access). For every u∈E, v∈F, and t>0, the oracle provides points pX(u,t)∈argminx∈X{tg(x)+12∥x−u∥2},pY(v,t)∈argminy∈Y{th(y)+12∥y−v∥2}. The oracle also returns Kx for any x∈E and K∗y for any y∈F. Each linear-map, adjoint, or proximal evaluation counts as one call to the same oracle. Proximal queries accept arbitrary real t, with the stated minimization requirement applying when t>0.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze Arrow–Hurwicz with a constant step size η>0 chosen from the available inputs. Starting from the given pair (x0,y0), the updates are xk+1=pX(xk−ηK∗yk,η),yk+1=pY(yk+ηKxk+1,η),k≥0. Each iteration makes four calls, in the order K∗yk, the primal proximal evaluation, Kxk+1, and the dual proximal evaluation. After N≥1 complete iterations, the output is x¯=1N∑k=1Nxk,y¯=1N∑k=1Nyk. If the call budget ends during a subsequent iteration, that incomplete iteration is excluded from the averages. If no iteration has been completed, the output is the current pair: (x0,y0) after zero or one call, and (x1,y0) after two or three calls.

The required accuracy is feasibility together with a uniform primal–dual gap bound: (x¯,y¯)∈X×Y,Φ(x¯,y)−Φ(x,y¯)≤εfor every x∈X, y∈Y,P-a.s., where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness; the specified Arrow–Hurwicz method and its oracle replies are deterministic.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Antonin Chambolle, Thomas Pock. A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging. 2011 (online publication 2010). Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) fixed exact operator and proximal oracle calls for a feasible averaged pair with uniform saddle gap at most ε, using primal–dual hybrid gradient; one call each to K, K∗, and the two proximal maps per iteration, with no initialization calls.
  • Antonin Chambolle, Thomas Pock. On the ergodic convergence rates of a first-order primal–dual algorithm. 2016 (online publication 2015; author manuscript HAL v2, September 28, 2015, used). Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) fixed exact operator and proximal oracle calls for a feasible averaged pair with uniform saddle gap at most ε, using their primal–dual algorithm with squared-norm proximity; one call each to K, K∗, and the two proximal maps per iteration, with no initialization calls.
theorems.formulaHtml: 4⋅⌈(11⋅R⋅(L⋅R+M)ε)43⌉+

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock. A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging. 2011 (May 2010 preprint used). Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) total exact proximal and K,K∗ oracle calls for uniform saddle gap at most ε, using their extrapolated primal-dual algorithm; fixed cost, two proximal calls and two operator applications per iteration.
  • Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock. On the ergodic convergence rates of a first-order primal-dual algorithm. 2016 (October 30, 2014 preprint used). Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) total exact proximal and K,K∗ oracle calls for uniform saddle gap at most ε, using their primal-dual algorithm with squared-norm proximity; fixed cost, two proximal calls and two operator applications per iteration.
theorems.formulaHtml: 4⋅⌈200⋅R⋅(L⋅R+M)ε⌉+

comparisonHtml:
Convex sets X⊂E, Y⊂F in real inner-product spaces satisfy ∥x∥,∥y∥≤R, with (x0,y0)∈X×Y. The objective is Φ(x,y)=g(x)+⟨y,Kx⟩−h(y), where K is continuous linear, ∥K∥≤L, and g,h are convex and M-Lipschitz on their respective domains; R,L,ε>0, M≥0. Exact K,K∗ and constrained proximal maps are available. The setup restricts algorithms to constant-step Arrow–Hurwicz. The target is a feasible pair (x¯,y¯) with Φ(x¯,y)−Φ(x,y¯)≤ε for every (x,y)∈X×Y, deterministically.

Bounded composite saddle problems: BoundedCompositeSaddle.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ArrowHurwiczUniformRate (Ours) (review) O(1+LR2+MRε)
(2) ArrowHurwiczBoundedSaddle (Ours) (review) O(1+(R(LR+M)ε)4/3)
(3) PDHG (Chambolle and Pock 2010, Thm. 1(b), Eq. (16)); θ=1. Derived bound. O(1+LR2ε) (1): Matches known rate when M≤LR, with an Arrow–Hurwicz guarantee. (2): No established improvement. (1): extra MR/ε. (2): worse accuracy exponent. (1), (2): require Lipschitz terms; (3) needs only bounded comparator sets.
(4) Arrow–Hurwicz (Chambolle and Pock 2010, sec. 3.2, Eq. (20)). Derived bound. O(1+L2R4ε2) For M≤LR, ε≤LR2, method-specific costs: (1) O(1+LR2/ε); (2) O(1+(LR2/ε)4/3), versus (4)’s quadratic dependence. (1): step independent of accuracy. (1), (2): add bounded primal domain and Lipschitz terms. (2) is worse when M≫L3/2R2/ε.
(5) AltGDA (Nan et al. 2026, Thm. 1, v1). Special case: simplices, g=h=0, R=1. O(1+Lδε); η=δ/(22L). (1): O(1+L/ε) removes 1/δ and knowledge of δ in the step. (1), (2): extend to bounded convex domains and Lipschitz composites. (2) gains when δ≪(ε/L)1/3, ε≤L. (1): larger leading constant for large δ. (2): worse when δ≫(ε/L)1/3.

Abbr: R bounds domain norms; L bounds ∥K∥; M bounds the Lipschitz constants; ε is the full saddle-gap tolerance. Costs count each K, K∗ and proximal evaluation separately (four calls per iteration, including two simplex projections in (5)). δ∈(0,1] is the minimum positive support probability and off-support payoff slack divided by L at a selected strictly complementary equilibrium, omitting absent off-support terms. Derived bounds specialize the cited comparator inequalities to radius R and the stated exact proximal oracles.

Chambolle, Antonin, and Thomas Pock. 2010. A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging. No. 685. Centre de Mathématiques Appliquées, École Polytechnique. https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/06/2646.pdf.
Nan, Tianlong, Garud Iyengar, Christian Kroer, and Shuvomoy Das Gupta. 2026. AltGDA Achieves Global O(1/T) Ergodic Convergence in Matrix Games. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.32995.
source:
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure

namespace OracleTemplate.ArrowHurwicz

universe u v

structure AHState (E : Type u) (F : Type v) where
  phase : ℕ
  x : E
  y : F
  v : E
  w : F
  sx : E
  sy : F
  n : ℕ

variable {E : Type u} {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

noncomputable def arrowHurwicz (η : ℝ) (x0 : E) (y0 : F) :
    Algorithm ((F ⊕ E) ⊕ ((E × ℝ) ⊕ (F × ℝ))) (E ⊕ F) (E × F) where
  State := AHState E F
  initial := fun _ => ⟨0, x0, y0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0⟩
  query :=  fun st => (0,
    if st.phase = 0 then Sum.inl (Sum.inl st.y)
    else if st.phase = 1 then Sum.inr (Sum.inl (st.x - η • st.v, η))
    else if st.phase = 2 then Sum.inl (Sum.inr st.x)
    else Sum.inr (Sum.inr (st.y + η • st.w, η)))
  update := fun st r =>
    if st.phase = 0 then ⟨1, st.x, st.y, Sum.elim id (fun _ => 0) r, st.w, st.sx, st.sy, st.n⟩
    else if st.phase = 1 then ⟨2, Sum.elim id (fun _ => 0) r, st.y, st.v, st.w, st.sx, st.sy, st.n⟩
    else if st.phase = 2 then ⟨3, st.x, st.y, st.v, Sum.elim (fun _ => 0) id r, st.sx, st.sy, st.n⟩
    else ⟨0, st.x, Sum.elim (fun _ => 0) id r, st.v, st.w, st.sx + st.x,
      st.sy + Sum.elim (fun _ => 0) id r, st.n + 1⟩
  output := fun st =>
    if st.n = 0 then (st.x, st.y) else (((st.n : ℝ))⁻¹ • st.sx, ((st.n : ℝ))⁻¹ • st.sy)

end OracleTemplate.ArrowHurwicz

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.BoundedCompositeSaddle

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.ArrowHurwicz

universe u

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  F : Type u
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [innerF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  X : Set E
  Y : Set F
  R : ℝ
  L : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E
  y0 : F

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.normedF Public.innerF

structure Problem (p : Public) where
  K : p.E →L[ℝ] p.F
  g : p.E → ℝ
  h : p.F → ℝ

def objective {p : Public} (I : Problem p) (x : p.E) (y : p.F) : ℝ :=
  I.g x + ⟪y, I.K x⟫ - I.h y

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance p := Problem p
  Query p := (p.F ⊕ p.E) ⊕ ((p.E × ℝ) ⊕ (p.F × ℝ))
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ p.F
  Output p := p.E × p.F
  publicInput := id
  valid p :=
    Convex ℝ p.X ∧ Convex ℝ p.Y ∧ p.x0 ∈ p.X ∧ p.y0 ∈ p.Y ∧
      (∀ x ∈ p.X, ‖x‖ ≤ p.R) ∧ (∀ y ∈ p.Y, ‖y‖ ≤ p.R) ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.M ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    ‖I.K‖ ≤ p.L ∧ ConvexOn ℝ p.X I.g ∧ ConvexOn ℝ p.Y I.h ∧
      (∀ a ∈ p.X, ∀ b ∈ p.X, |I.g a - I.g b| ≤ p.M * ‖a - b‖) ∧
      (∀ a ∈ p.Y, ∀ b ∈ p.Y, |I.h a - I.h b| ≤ p.M * ‖a - b‖) ∧
      ∃ (adj : p.F → p.E) (proxX : p.E × ℝ → p.E) (proxY : p.F × ℝ → p.F),
        (∀ y z, ⟪adj y, z⟫ = ⟪y, I.K z⟫) ∧
        (∀ q : p.E × ℝ, 0 < q.2 → proxX q ∈ p.X ∧ ∀ w ∈ p.X,
          q.2 * I.g (proxX q) + ‖proxX q - q.1‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ q.2 * I.g w + ‖w - q.1‖ ^ 2 / 2) ∧
        (∀ q : p.F × ℝ, 0 < q.2 → proxY q ∈ p.Y ∧ ∀ w ∈ p.Y,
          q.2 * I.h (proxY q) + ‖proxY q - q.1‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ q.2 * I.h w + ‖w - q.1‖ ^ 2 / 2) ∧
        (∀ k s y, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl (Sum.inl y))) s = Sum.inl (adj y)) ∧
        (∀ k s x, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl (Sum.inr x))) s = Sum.inr (I.K x)) ∧
        (∀ k s q, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr (Sum.inl q))) s = Sum.inl (proxX q)) ∧
        (∀ k s q, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr (Sum.inr q))) s = Sum.inr (proxY q))
  successful p I output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), (output ω).1 ∈ p.X ∧ (output ω).2 ∈ p.Y ∧
      ∀ x ∈ p.X, ∀ y ∈ p.Y, objective I (output ω).1 y - objective I x (output ω).2 ≤ p.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A := ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ A = arrowHurwicz η p.x0 p.y0

end LongTails.Setups.BoundedCompositeSaddle
